explain.curious: In a pair, both bodies pull on each other, so the orbit depends on their combined mass.
explain.science: The two-body problem reduces to one body moving under the total mass G(M + m).

references: Murray, C. D. and Dermott, S. F. 1999, Solar System Dynamics, Cambridge University Press. doi:10.1017/CBO9781139174817

equation.name: Length of a year
equation.formula: P = 2 * pi * sqrt(a * a * a / (G * M))

source.text: Murray, C. D. and Dermott, S. F. 1999, Solar System Dynamics, Cambridge University Press

explain.curious: The farther out a world orbits, the longer its year, and not just in proportion: four times farther means eight times longer.
explain.science: Kepler's third law for two point masses, using the sum of both masses. Exact for an isolated pair; other bodies perturb it slightly.
